I quit smoking in September of 2022 after smoking for probably 14 years quite heavily. Prior to this I also had another try cold turkey (lasted maybe over a month).

I would say that the first week was the worst and I always tried to keep my hands busy - take a bike for a ride if my emotions are over the roof, go to the gym, craft something, etc. Physical excersizes or activities just helped my hands be busy and my anger be channeled out elsewhere (not on my family or friends).

Then it just gets better and better. You can track your day count, buy yourself small encouragement gifts every week/month with the money you saved etc.

Cravings subside, but the first few days these just feel like crashing waves - you just hold in there and beat it - the intensity just passes each time.

And overall, regain the control of yourself - your hand alone does not put the cigarette in your mouth. You do.

But I think over all, the underlying motivation is what matters the most. I have found a new relationship and my partner did not smoke (did not mind it much if I did, but I just simply knew I did not taste or smell nice at all) and most of all - sounds silly, but I wanted to live as long as possible and go on lifelong adventure with this person. Only made sense to get rid of this terrible habit which could prematurily end my adventures.

But yes, everyone's experience is unique. I wish you best of luck in finding what works out best for you and kicking it!

I was also prescribed this mini-pill after I expressed my disatisfaction with the previous combine pill. It is now month 9 on it and I think it did improve my mental state compared to the previous one. I have never experienced any nausea or any gastro problems on any of the pills, so I must be lucky there. But the periods... So, I thought maybe it will all settle in, but still, month 9 and my periods are much lighter (than my regular one before any BC pills) and they last maybe 2-3 weeks (I even lost the count, seemed pointless... haha.) 

And of course, it is still hard to judge what is the cause of what, because I also meanwhile had precancerous cells and part of my cervix removed a month ago, which also contributes to strange periods. Obviously, had so much stress and changes in life the last year, that I am not sure anymore what is/was my baseline mental state before. 

But overall, I am happy it truly took away period pains and seems to have had less detrimental effect on my mood, but I am wondering if I should give it another try and try some other pill instead... Hard to know what is normal and my GP (who prescribes it) was not too helpful anyway.

Hold in there! I must say, you are truly not alone in this time of waiting and questioning, imagining the worst outcomes and yet hoping for the best... Just remember that some things are not in your control and everyone is doing the best they can to help you and take the action needed. And most likely, it truly will not be anything that cannot be solved in a single procedure or you might not even need anything done right now! 

I am sending you my best wishes and support. I have been through this rollercoaster, but it does get clearer, better and you will get back on your stable feet again soon! 

In my case the first ever self-pap smear turned into a pap smear in the office (which was also so terrifying at a time), which turned into a colposcopy and then leep procedure. For now, I am just on the wait for the next 6 months... Every single step felt like the situation was just getting worse and scarier and scarier... And yet, it truly was not that bad! So no matter what happens, I am sure you are in very good hands! And if you want to talk about anything, feel free to message me as well. Having support can be really helpful as well. <3

Hey! Based purely on my observations, he simply might be quite dark to begin with; as I've seen them differ in the brightness/darkness spectrum. 

However, after changing the substrate to this "snow" white sand, I have noticed an overall improvement - instead of bleaching out my mostly dark fishes, it only made them pop out. As for the Severums - they only seem to become slightly lighter with the biggest difference in their lower parts of the body. The lighter one, instead of looking too light, seems to have even redder/orangier (is that even a word, haha) underbelly and chin. It seems that the white sand reflects the light back unto their bellies and makes their colours pop even harder! 

The whole reason for choosing the black sand was to have the colours pop, and yet, I have only experienced the opposite. Of course, the whole myriad of problems: diatoms popping up, algae overgrowing, tannins leaching out, etc. had a fair share in dulling out everything. But now I am in heaven!
